title: Network Map

story.briefing: The Core network has no map. Before anything can be routed through it, someone has to count how many links each node actually carries.
story.success: Network mapped. Every node knows how many neighbours it has.

description: A graph is given as n, the number of nodes numbered 0 to n-1, and edges, an array of [u, v] pairs. Edges are undirected unless stated otherwise, and there are no self-loops or duplicate edges. Return an array of length n where each entry is the number of edges touching that node. A node with no edges has 0.

examples.explanation: Node 1 sits between the other two.

hints: Each edge is a fact about two nodes at once, so a single pass over the edges can update both ends.
Scanning the whole edge list once per node re-reads everything n times. Walk the edges once instead and let each one update the counts it affects.
Start an array of n zeros. For every [u, v] edge, increment the entry at u and the entry at v. Return the array.
